I attached a short benchmark deck that shows our internal rerank baselines and a sample query CSV. If that looks good, Aditya and I will schedule the benchmark runs; Sean will help with onboarding and infra access if you want us to run tests in your cloud account.

- If cost matters, show unit economics: cost per 100k queries and cost per million stored vectors with/without PQ.

Hey Emma — quick technical thoughts on your questions: 

1) Disk-backed IVF+PQ: yes — IVF+PQ on disk is a common production pattern. Expect slightly higher p95 vs memory HNSW, but with appropriate shard sizing and prefetching we often see p95 retrievals in the 30–100ms range for 10M–50M corpora (depending on hardware). If you need consistent single-digit ms p95, that generally requires keeping the active working set in RAM on optimized nodes (or using our Dedicated GPU pools which give lower latency for hybrid rerank flows).

2) PQ and recall: product quantization introduces approximation and can reduce recall for the first-pass retrieval. For reranking pipelines, a common pattern is: use a compressed index (IVF+PQ) for candidate retrieval (k=100–200) then run a higher-fidelity reranker on the top candidates. With that approach, PQ’s impact on final recall@10 is often small. We recommend measuring recall@100 on the index stage and recall@10 after rerank.

3) Costs (very rough ballpark estimates):
- Storage: 25M vectors @1536 dims ~= 25M * 1536 * 4 bytes = ~153GB raw (float32). With PQ (8-bit), storage can drop by ~4-8x depending on config. Managed vector DB storage + replication: ballpark $200–600/month for that dataset on a managed service; self-hosted infra costs vary.
- Embedding compute: generating 25M vectors at 1536 dims is the main one-time cost; for a streaming POC (10k sample) negligible. For per-100k queries (inference + retrieval + rerank): expect $X–Y depending on reranker size. We’ll provide a detailed cost table after the sample run.

Recommended test matrix we’ll run for you: 
A) Embeddings dims: 512 vs 1536
B) Index types: HNSW (in-memory) vs IVF+PQ (disk)
C) Retrieval k: 10, 50, 100 (measure recall@1/5/10 and recall@100)
D) Reranker: lightweight MLP ranker vs full cross-attention reranker (end-to-end latency)

Deliverables: benchmark spreadsheet with recall curves, p50/p95 latencies, and a per-100k queries cost breakdown, plus reproducible scripts we can share.

If that all looks good I’ll queue the runs and we can align on whether Redwood runs them from our hosted env or on ShortStack cloud creds.
